source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: GPT-style models are trained on images using self-supervised learning, the same general method Session 3 introduced for text. What does that look like when applied to images, as described in the lecture?

options.text: Images and text are folded into one shared sequence from the start, with pieces of that sequence left out for the model to predict
options.feedback: This is the native multimodal approach the lecture describes: text and images are part of the same training process from day one, treated as a shared sequence rather than two separate pipelines bolted together.

options.text: A separate model is trained only on images, then combined with the text model afterward through a projection step
options.feedback: That describes the other approach the lecture contrasts this with -- the Anthropic-style method of pretraining on text first and adding vision later. It is a real approach, just not this one.

options.text: Human labelers write captions for each image, and the model is trained to reproduce those captions
options.feedback: Writing captions for supervision is a plausible-sounding training method, but it is ordinary supervised learning with human labels, not the self-supervised, predict-the-missing-piece method the lecture describes.

options.text: An already-trained language model is simply shown static images afterward and asked to describe them, with no additional training involved
options.feedback: That describes using a finished model at inference time, not training it. Both approaches the lecture discusses involve real training on image data, whether jointly from the start or in a later step.
